findings.title: Customer & Partner Updates: Remote Code Execution Vulnerability in PTC's Windchill and FlexPLM Solutions
findings.summary_md: PTC's Trust Center advisory for CVE-2026-12569, a critical vulnerability that could allow an unauthorized user to execute code remotely in Windchill and FlexPLM. Remediation steps were posted June 17, 2026, per-version patches shipped from June 18, and the complete patch set arrived July 14. The page carries the campaign IoCs PTC kept expanding: C2 IP 5.180.41.35, hex-named JSP webshells under /Windchill/login/, the malicious X-windchill-req header, and a webshell SHA-256 of 55a1eb4c2d3da04376df39d7ba832569c6af1a37a0cf2b95f754ac898023a30c.

findings.title: CVE-2026-12569 Detail (NVD)
findings.summary_md: NVD's record describes a critical RCE in PTC Windchill PDMLink and PTC FlexPLM exploitable through deserialization of untrusted data, scored 9.3 Critical (CVSS v4) by CNA PTC, with CWE-20 and CWE-502 and affected builds spanning releases prior to 11.0 M030 through 13.1.3. It records the CISA KEV addition on June 25, 2026 with a federal remediation due date of June 28, 2026.

findings.title: Cl0p Exploitation of PTC Windchill & FlexPLM (CVE-2026-12569)
findings.summary_md: Ransom-ISAC's coordinated threat advisory with eCrime.ch and DEFUSED assesses that Cl0p exploited CVE-2026-12569 as a zero-day in early June 2026, chaining a pre-authentication FlexPLM WSDL information disclosure (CVSS 7.5) with the Windchill login servlet flaw for unauthenticated RCE (CVSS 9.8). It documents extortion emails sent from July 20, 2026 with the subject line Windchill PDMLink module serious data leak, confirms victim sectors of manufacturing, automotive, aerospace, and retail/apparel, and as of July 22 noted Cl0p had not yet listed victims on its leak site. Includes a structural YARA rule for the JSP webshells and an incident-observed C2 at 79.141.160.78.

findings.title: Clop Returns with Custom Implant in Mass-Extortion Campaign
findings.summary_md: ReliaQuest Threat Research (authors John Dilgen and Connor Short) dissects the custom Windchill web shell deployed after CVE-2026-12569 exploitation: a single S command decrypts the application keystore and returns LDAP manager and administrative credentials in plaintext, a built-in Java class loader runs attacker-supplied bytecode entirely in memory, and vault enumeration writes a repository map to flst.txt. Commands ride the X-windchill-req header with GZIP-compressed responses, and the report publishes implant SHA-256 321e1fb01eb3462b48ff6ccdef132acc1182e3f7456548439f0d4ead12fd98bf. ReliaQuest assesses with moderate confidence that copycat actors will adopt the vulnerability as public exploit code spreads.
